root_cause: PULPHardwareLoops::getLoopTripCount (inlined into convertToHardwareLoop) called MRI->getVRegDef(R)->getParent() on the loop's start/end operand without checking that it is a virtual register. RISC-V ISel selects compare-with-0 as the physical $x0 (upstream 450edb0b3766, RISCVInstrInfo.td:1592-1594), so every count-down-to-zero latch ('BNE/BEQ %iv.next, $x0', produced by LSR from ordinary for-loops) returned a null def and segfaulted. The code was copied from HexagonHardwareLoops, which has no zero register.
fix: If the start/end operand is a physical register, accept it only when checkForImmediate proves a constant ($x0 = 0; computeCount already handles this case by copying $x0 into a vreg and using the original counter as the trip count) and do not queue it in OldInsts. Any other physical register has an unknown value at the preheader, so no hardware loop is formed (same rule as the existing checkForImmediate and HexagonHardwareLoops::checkForImmediate:1550). Virtual registers take exactly the previous path.

other_errors_seen: Missed optimisation, not a crash: computeCount's constant-bounds path (startIsImm && endIsImm) accepts only Cmp == EQ and declines NE latches. So constant-count loops whose latch is 'BNE %iv.next, $x0' to the header (for example the ten 100-iteration loops left after -O2 unrolls the inner loop of a nested constant-count loop, and notes/20/F003-repro/reduced.ll) get no hardware loop. The path also does not check whether the branch target is the header or the exit. Candidate for a separate task.

Missed optimisation: an inner loop without a dedicated preheader is declined ('loop has no preheader', FIXME in convertToHardwareLoop), e.g. nested3 in the scratch tests, so only the outer level gets a hardware loop.
